---
title: "Reference"
subtitle: "Every option the invoice format accepts."
description: "The complete invoice configuration: sender and recipient, the invoice block and its line items, bank details, currency handling, and validation."
---

## Using the format

```yaml
format: invoice-typst
```

```bash
quarto render invoice.qmd --to invoice-typst
```

## The document

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | Set above the totals table, as a heading. |
| `description` | Set under the title, in italics. Read only when `title` is set. |
| `logo` | A path to an image, set beside the invoice details. Falls back to `brand.logo`. |
| `papersize` | The paper. `a4` unless set. |
| `margin` | A mapping of Typst page margins, `x` and `y` by default. |
| `lang`, `region` | Passed to Typst. `lang` also chooses the number separators and the language of the labels. |
| `mainfont`, `fontsize` | Fall back to `brand.typography.base.family` and `.size`. Without either, the font is New Computer Modern, which Typst includes, at 12pt. |

: Options outside the three blocks. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

## Sender and recipient

Both are required, and rendering fails without them.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `sender.name` | Required. |
| `sender.email` | Set as a `mailto:` link. |
| `sender.registration` | Company registration number. |
| `sender.vat` | VAT number. |
| `sender.exempted` | The wording of a VAT exemption notice, set in grey under the totals. |
| `sender.address` | `street`, `zip`, `city`, `state`, `country`. |
| `recipient.name` | Required. |
| `recipient.address` | The same address fields. |

: The two parties. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

## The invoice block

Required, along with `invoice.number`, `invoice.issued`, and `invoice.due`.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invoice.number` | | The invoice number. |
| `invoice.issued` | | Issue date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `invoice.due` | | Due date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `invoice.reference` | | A payment reference for the transfer. Set in the bank block, so it appears only when `bank` is given. |
| `invoice.currency` | `EUR` | An ISO 4217 code, `GBP` for example. |
| `invoice.fee` | `2.28` | A late payment fee, as a percentage. |
| `invoice.penalty` | `€40` | Recovery costs, set as written. |
| `invoice.items` | | The line items. See below. |

: The invoice block. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[22,12,66]"}

::: {.callout-warning}
`invoice.penalty` reaches Typst as a string whatever it is written as, so a number is set as a bare figure rather than in the invoice currency: `penalty: 40` on a `GBP` invoice reads `40`, not `£40`.
Write the amount with its symbol, as `penalty: "£40"`.
The default when it is left out is the literal `€40`, in every currency.
:::

### Line items

```yaml
invoice:
  items:
    - description: Strategy workshop
      details: Two-day on-site facilitation.
      quantity: 2
      unit-price: 1500
      vat: 20
```

| Field | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | | A short description. Required. |
| `details` | | A longer one, set below the item. |
| `quantity` | `1` | |
| `unit-price` | `0` | Excluding VAT. |
| `vat` | `0` | The rate, as a percentage. |

: The fields of a line item. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[20,12,68]"}

The subtotal excluding VAT, the VAT, and the grand total are computed from these.
A quantity that is a whole number is set without a decimal part, and the VAT rate is set as a whole percentage.

::: {.callout-note}
Leave `invoice.items` out and the body of the document is rendered in its place instead, which is how a hand-written Typst table is kept working.
:::

## Bank details

`bank.bic` and `bank.iban`, set under a payment heading at the foot of the page along with `invoice.reference`.

::: {.callout-important}
Both keys have to be present.
An invoice with no `bank` block fails to compile, so give the block even when the payment details are not yet known.
:::

## Currency

Amounts are formatted with the decimal and thousand separators of the document's `lang`, so the same figures read correctly in English and in French.

Twenty-six ISO 4217 codes carry a symbol, `EUR`, `USD`, `GBP`, `JPY`, and `CHF` among them.
A code with no symbol is set as the code followed by a space.

`SEK`, `NOK`, `DKK`, `PLN`, `CZK`, and `CHF` put the symbol after the amount; every other currency puts it before.

## Language

The format sets each label and sentence from a Quarto [`language`](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/language.html) key.
English is the default.
The format also includes French translations, which it uses when `lang: fr` is set.
Any other `lang` value gives the English text.

To change one string, set its key under your language code:

```yaml
lang: fr
sender:
  registration: "12245/FR12334"
language:
  fr:
    invoice-registration: "SIREN/SIRET"
```

The invoice then shows `SIREN/SIRET: 12245/FR12334`.
The other French strings do not change.

::: {.callout-important}
Put each key under the language code that matches `lang`, for example `fr:` or `en:`.
With Quarto 1.10, Quarto ignores a key at the top level of `language`.
:::

You can also keep your strings in a translation file.
Give the path of the file as the value of `language`, and put the keys under the language code in the file:

```yaml
lang: fr
language: my-labels.yml
```

```{.yaml filename="my-labels.yml"}
fr:
  invoice-registration: "SIREN/SIRET"
en:
  invoice-registration: "Company number"
```

The values in the file replace the values of the format for the same keys.
Quarto 1.11.4 and later also read one file for each language next to the main file, for example `my-labels-fr.yml` with the keys at the top level.

| Key | English default |
| --- | --- |
| `invoice-title` | `Invoice` |
| `invoice-registration` | `Registration number` |
| `invoice-vat-number` | `VAT number` |
| `invoice-number` | `Invoice number` |
| `invoice-issued` | `Issued on` |
| `invoice-due` | `Payment due date` |
| `invoice-payment-title` | `Payment information` |
| `invoice-reference` | `Reference` |
| `invoice-reference-note` | `To be used as label on your bank transfer to identify the transaction.` |
| `invoice-item-details` | `Details` |
| `invoice-item-quantity` | `Qty` |
| `invoice-item-unit-price` | `Unit price` |
| `invoice-item-vat` | `VAT %` |
| `invoice-item-total` | `Total excl. VAT` |
| `invoice-total-excl` | `Total excl. VAT` |
| `invoice-total-vat` | `VAT` |
| `invoice-total-incl` | `Total` |
| `invoice-terms` | The payment terms at the foot of the page. |
| `invoice-months` | `January, February, ..., December` |
| `invoice-date` | `the {day}{ordinal} of {month}, {year}` |
| `invoice-ordinals` | `st, nd, rd, th, ...` |

: The language keys. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[34,66]"}

`invoice-title` is the first word of the PDF title, before the invoice number.
The French values are in [`_extension.yml`](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-invoice/blob/main/_extensions/invoice/_extension.yml).

`invoice-terms` uses these placeholders: `{sender}`, `{date}`, `{days}`, `{fee}`, and `{penalty}`.
The format replaces each placeholder with its value.
You can change the order of the placeholders to suit the grammar of your language.

The date of issue in `invoice-terms` comes from three keys:

- `invoice-months` gives the twelve month names, separated by commas.
- `invoice-ordinals` gives the suffix for each day of the month, separated by commas. When the list has fewer than 31 items, the last item applies to the remaining days.
- `invoice-date` puts the parts together with the placeholders `{day}`, `{ordinal}`, `{month}`, and `{year}`.

The French values give `1er janvier 2026`.

An empty value gives the English text.
To remove the suffix after the day, remove `{ordinal}` from `invoice-date`.

::: {.callout-warning}
Do not use a backtick (`` ` ``) in a value.
This character stops the Typst compilation.
All other characters, quotation marks and backslashes included, appear as you write them.
:::

## Validation

::: {.callout-important}
`invoice.issued` and `invoice.due` must both be `YYYY-MM-DD`, and `invoice.due` must fall on or after `invoice.issued`.
Either mistake raises an error while rendering rather than producing a document nobody would notice was wrong.
:::

## Branding

The format reads [`_brand.yml`](https://posit-dev.github.io/brand-yml/) for the logo, the base font and size, and the heading family, weight, style, colour, and line height:

```yaml
brand:
  typography:
    fonts:
      - family: Alegreya Sans
        source: google
    base:
      family: "Alegreya Sans"
      size: 12pt
    headings:
      family: "Alegreya Sans"
      color: dodgerblue
```

A self-contained example lives under [`examples/`](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-invoice/tree/main/examples) in the repository.

## Limitations

- PDF through Typst only.
- The totals table is generated from `invoice.items`; mixing it with a hand-written table means choosing one or the other.
- The format includes English and French text only. For another language, set each key under the code of that language.
- The format makes a PDF only. It does not make a structured electronic invoice, such as Factur-X, UBL, or CII.

::: {.callout-warning title="Electronic invoicing in France"}
From 1 September 2027, all businesses in France must issue electronic invoices for sales to other businesses subject to VAT in France.
These invoices go through an approved platform (*plateforme agréée*) in a structured format.
For these sales, a PDF from this format is not a valid invoice.

Sales to private customers and to customers outside France are not in the scope of electronic invoicing.
For these sales, the PDF stays valid, and you send the sale data to the tax administration through e-reporting.

Large and mid-sized businesses have had these obligations since 1 September 2026.
Support for Factur-X is tracked in [#47](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-invoice/issues/47).
:::
